title_guess: Inflation tax and inflation gap: closing a fiscal deficit openly by taxes or silently by printing money
recurring_cast: real_person_photo of a head of government standing for 'the government' in every frame (BIE will not use it)
budget_briefcase (document with a BUDGET stamp and a rupee briefcase)
two budget bars: long red 'Estimated Expenditures' over a shorter green 'Estimated Receipts' whose missing end is a hatched yellow GAP block = FISCAL DEFICIT
column of five hands holding rupee notes at the right edge = the people's pockets
rupee_note fan (money taken in by tax, later printed money)
sign_badge: green + on the government's money, red - on every hand
tax_badge 'TAX' beside each hand, renamed 'INFLATION TAX'
running_examples: no numbers anywhere: the one running picture is the budget bar with its gap, closed first by taxes, then (after a rewind to the same gap) by printed money
the same five hands lose in both routes (TAX tags, then INFLATION TAX tags) and the government gains in both

best_moments.why: the gap closes, then a green + arrow carries the money to the government while a red - lands on every hand, on 'the government got more, our pockets got less': gainer and loser in one picture
the printing-money route ends in the same picture as the tax route (same hands, same TAX tags, same red minus marks), so 'it is exactly like a tax' is shown by reusing the earlier scene
the 'INCREASE TAX' bubble of the open route is answered by a 'Shhh!' in the hidden route: the whole difference between a tax and an inflation tax is one swapped bubble
the TAX tags beside the hands turn into INFLATION TAX exactly on the spoken term
the opening shows the idea before any term: notes in the people's hands get a red -, notes held by the government get a green +
the canvas rewinds to the open gap before the second route, so both routes start from the same problem and can be compared

weak_moments.why: the four routes of deficit financing are a text-only fork and three of them drop away without explanation; 15 s of speech here (107.9-122.9 s) is missing from the transcript, so it cannot be checked that they were named
inflation is only a red word under an arrow; prices rising is never drawn (no price tag or basket getting dearer), so 'purchasing power falls' is carried by minus signs alone
seigniorage is a grey text box ('profit from issuing currency'); the gain is not shown (for example printing cost vs face value)

doubtful: the fiscal-deficit gap is renamed 'inflation gap' and the voice says filling it always brings inflation, which contradicts the tax route shown earlier without inflation; an inflationary gap usually means demand above full-employment output. Verify before reuse
fiscal deficit is drawn as expenditure minus receipts without saying that borrowings are left out of receipts (with borrowings counted the budget always balances)
a real person's photo stands for the government throughout; BIE should use a generic government figure or building

segments.teaches: inflation tax is money the government takes out of people's pockets without telling them

elements.what: real photo of a head of government (later holding a fan of rupee notes)
INFLATION TAX
hands holding rupee notes in a column at the right edge
green + on the government's notes, red - on each hand

segments.notes: 4 change events in 12 s. The idea is shown before it is explained: minus on the people's notes, plus on the government's notes, on 'takes money from our pocket'. Real person photo: note it, BIE will not use it.
segments.idea: a hidden tax: the government's money grows while people's money shrinks, and nobody announces it
segments.shown_as: a photo standing for the government sits beside the title INFLATION TAX; a column of five hands holding rupee notes slides in at the right edge; the government figure now holds a fan of notes, then a green + lands on that fan and a red - on every hand

segments.teaches: every year the budget lists planned expenditures and expected receipts; the shortfall between them is the fiscal deficit; the government must raise receipts to close it

elements.what: the same government photo, now at top left without notes
budget document with a BUDGET stamp and a rupee briefcase
long red bar 'Estimated Expenditures' over a shorter green bar 'Estimated Receipts'
hatched yellow GAP block filling the missing end of the green bar
FISCAL DEFICIT under the gap
black arrow drawn through the gap from the end of receipts to the end of expenditures
FISCAL DEFICIT struck through

segments.notes: 6 change events. The arrow through the gap and the strike on FISCAL DEFICIT appear between 50 and 60 s without a detected event (seen on the 59.7 s frame), around 'raise receipts and end this gap'. The transcript loses about 12 s of speech (31.8-43.6 s) just before 'gap' is named. Definition is loose: textbooks exclude borrowings from receipts.
segments.idea: fiscal deficit is the gap left when planned spending is longer than expected income
segments.shown_as: a budget document with a rupee briefcase pops in beside the government figure; a long red Estimated Expenditures bar draws out of it, then a shorter green Estimated Receipts bar under it; the missing end of the green bar fills with a hatched yellow GAP block labelled FISCAL DEFICIT; then an arrow runs through the gap and FISCAL DEFICIT is struck as the voice says the gap must be closed

segments.teaches: route 1: the government raises existing taxes or imposes new ones and announces them; people pay more, receipts grow and the gap closes; the government gains and people's pockets lose

elements.what: '(By Increasing Tax)' under Estimated Receipts
the five hands with notes slide back in at the right
'INCREASE TAX' speech bubble at the government figure
TAX beside each hand
fan of rupee notes under the receipts bar
green receipts bar grows to the full length of the red bar; GAP and FISCAL DEFICIT vanish
green elbow arrow with a + from the notes back up to the government
red - on each hand

segments.notes: 8 change events (about every 5 s). The tax route is drawn as a loop: announcement bubble, TAX tags on the payers, their notes under the receipts bar, the bar grows over the gap, then + to the government and - to the people on the exact words. '(By Increasing Tax)' appears around 61 s without a detected event.
segments.idea: an open tax closes the gap by moving money from people to the government, and the government says so
segments.shown_as: '(By Increasing Tax)' writes under the receipts bar; the hands with notes slide back in; an 'INCREASE TAX' bubble pops from the government figure and a TAX tag appears beside each hand; a fan of notes appears under the receipts bar and the green bar grows to the length of the red bar, wiping out the GAP; a green elbow arrow with a + runs from the notes up to the government while a red - lands on every hand

segments.teaches: route 2: deficit financing, whose ways are external aid, external borrowing, internal borrowing and printing money; the video follows printing money

elements.what: the budget bars rewind to the open GAP with FISCAL DEFICIT (bubble, tags, grown bar removed)
down-arrow from FISCAL DEFICIT to DEFICIT FINANCING
DEFICIT FINANCING forks into External Aids, External Borrowings, Internal Borrowing and Printing Money (green)
fan of rupee notes beside Printing Money once the other three branches drop away

segments.notes: 4 change events. The canvas rewinds to the problem state before the second route. Transcript gap 107.9-122.9 s: the branch names and the reason for choosing printing money are not in the recognised words.
segments.idea: a second way to fill the gap is deficit financing, and printing money is one of its routes
segments.shown_as: the tax bubble, tags and grown bar vanish and the budget bars return with the open GAP and FISCAL DEFICIT; an arrow drops to DEFICIT FINANCING, which forks into four labelled routes; three routes fall away, leaving Printing Money, and a fan of notes appears beside it

segments.teaches: printed money reaches the government and covers the deficit, but more money in the economy brings inflation, which cuts people's purchasing power: the same result as a tax

elements.what: green elbow arrow with a + from the printed notes up to the budget
down-arrow from Printing Money to a red INFLATION
the five hands with notes return at the right
TAX beside each hand
red - on each hand

segments.notes: 5 change events. The tax route's ending (hands, TAX tags, minus marks) is reused for the printing route, so 'this is just like a tax' is shown about 2 s before it is said. Inflation itself is a red word; rising prices are never drawn.
segments.idea: printing money to fill the gap makes prices rise, so people lose buying power just as if they had paid a tax
segments.shown_as: a green elbow arrow with a + rises from the printed notes to the budget; an arrow drops from Printing Money to a red INFLATION; the hands with notes slide back in, TAX tags appear beside them just before the voice compares this to the tax case, and red minus marks land on every hand as the voice says people's purchasing power fell

segments.teaches: the difference: a tax is announced, inflation is not; this hidden tax is the inflation tax; the money the government gains by issuing currency is seigniorage

elements.what: 'Shhh!' beside the government figure
each TAX tag becomes INFLATION TAX
'(Seigniorage)' under the green + arrow
grey box: profit the government makes by issuing currency

segments.notes: 3 change events. The open 'INCREASE TAX' bubble of route 1 returns as 'Shhh!'; the tags are renamed on the spoken term. Seigniorage is recognised as 'sign or range'. The video treats the inflation-tax money and seigniorage as one; textbooks keep them related but distinct.
segments.idea: inflation tax is a tax nobody announced; what the government earns from issuing money is called seigniorage
segments.shown_as: a 'Shhh!' appears beside the government figure on 'without saying anything'; each TAX tag beside the losing hands becomes INFLATION TAX as the term is spoken; '(Seigniorage)' writes under the green + arrow that carried money to the government, and a grey box defines it as profit from issuing currency

segments.teaches: the fiscal-deficit gap is also called the inflation gap, because filling it brings inflation

segments.idea: the same budget gap gets a second name, inflation gap, because filling it can push prices up
